properties.statement: [BL-154] Skills are read once per 380 tool calls, and the skill for the tool used 92 times has never been read at all
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Measured 2026-08-01 by tools/surface_usage.py, the sixth instrument and the first to measure the SURFACE rather than the engine \u2014 46 retained Claude Code transcripts, 2026-07-18 to 2026-08-01, 6,095 reflow2 tool calls across 10 projects. Anthony's idea.* 16 get_skill calls in 6,095 tool calls. Eleven of fifteen skills fetched at all, and none more than twice across 46 sessions. NEVER FETCHED: link-artifacts, report-friction, ci-gate, kpp-proposal. The link-artifacts case is the sharpest, because it is not a case of an unused feature: link_artifact was called 92 times and set_artifact_checksum 408 times across 22 sessions \u2014 the WORK the skill covers is among the most-performed in the whole dataset, and its skill has never once been read. Whatever that skill knows is not reaching the agent doing the thing. report-friction is the same shape from the other side: friction gets filed constantly (BL-114..BL-152 are largely friction reports) and the skill telling you how to file it has never been opened. This is req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session with a number attached at last \u2014 that requirement exists because skill use was believed to decay, and the decay is now measured rather than suspected. It is also the counterpart to [BL-152]: that item found a served skill whose text had rotted; this one finds that almost nobody would have read it either way. Fix shapes: (1) the honest cheap one \u2014 the served tool descriptions already carry one-sentence conventions for a few tools ([the tool-carries-convention verification] is planned for exactly this), so extend that to the tools whose skills are never read, since the tool description IS read every session and the skill is not; (2) situation-shaped triggers, which is cap:skill-triggers, already planned and unbuilt \u2014 and this measurement is the evidence for prioritising it; (3) accept that skills are documentation for humans rather than instructions for agents, and stop counting on them \u2014 which would be a real decision and should be made deliberately if the numbers do not move. Do NOT respond by nagging: ver:skill-triggers's own counterweight says a trigger that fires on correct work is the BL-23/BL-42 failure, and one read per 380 calls will not be fixed by more reminders. Size M CORROBORATED THE SAME DAY, and it is the sharpest evidence this row could have had. Hours after cap:gap-carries-a-reading was BUILT \u2014 its six obligations written into detect-and-ask and enforced by skill_lint \u2014 the agent that wrote them went on putting decisions to Anthony as prose, until he pointed it out: *\"we joked that this should be a reflow2 skill and I even think we recorded this, but I'm still having to remind you.\"* The skill existed, was correct, was enforced, and did not reach the session that authored it. That is this row's claim at its strongest: not that skills go unread by the inattentive, but that WRITING one does not make it operative even for its own author. It is also the argument for [BL-152]'s sibling fix \u2014 the convention that rides the TOOL arrives with every call, and a rule that lives only in a skill depends on someone choosing to load it. When the format was finally used, both questions were answered in one reply with the recommendation taken \u2014 versus the prose versions, which had produced several rounds of clarification. One observation, not a measurement, and recorded as such.", "origin": "Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-154 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: M."}
